verdicts.misleading_risk: Moderate if done carelessly. The licence holder line and year ('Copyright (c) 2026 Cell Migration Lab') and any licence for text or artwork are owner decisions. Other repos use 2025 or 2026 and one (GuessTheCondition) has a different holder style, so copying a line is a guess. Rewording the footer to 'The LabConstrictor template is MIT licensed' would itself assert a fact about a different repo (it is true: LabConstrictor/LICENSE is MIT), but it is a content change nobody asked for.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Build only the uncontroversial part once an owner confirms the holder and year: add LICENSE (MIT) to CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor-Site; the footer sentence 'Open source, MIT licensed.' then becomes true for the site code and needs no rewording. Add a 3-line 'Licence' section to README.md: 'Site code: MIT (see LICENSE). Text, logo and comic: terms not yet stated (see Credits).' Do not invent a text licence or put CC terms anywhere until the owners choose; do not touch the footer wording unless the owners want it to point at /credits/. No new test needed (a LICENSE-exists test is over-engineering).
verdicts.evidence: Verified: no LICENSE file in /home/user/labconstrictor-site; gh api repos/CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor-Site returns license=None, visibility=public. Footer text at overrides/main.html:89 reads 'Open source, MIT licensed.' and renders on the built site/index.html. README has no licence section (grep). Template and 9 other repos have LICENSE (MIT; holders 'Cell Migration Lab', years 2025 or 2026; GuessTheCondition uses a 'The MIT License (MIT)' header without that line); LabConstrictor-QuPath has none. mkdocs.yml has extra.listed false, so the site is currently unlisted, which lowers urgency but the repo is public.

verdicts.misleading_risk: High if the credit is guessed. The git history only shows uploader Ivan Hidalgo (commits a052fc0, c92298a, e0eb33a, 62b59d1 on origin/doc_source for logo and comic); that proves upload, not creation. The logo PNG info has only Software='www.inkscape.org' (export tool), no author or licence. The site's lc.css says 'hand-drawn', which is the only statement of origin and is not evidenced. Any name, rights holder or licence must come from the owners, never from the commit author. The Demo repo copy (app/logo/logo.png) is a separate export, so 'master file' really is open.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do not build code first. Step 1: send the owners the question list (creator or 'unknown', rights holder, licence, permission for apps built from the template to reuse the logo given LabConstrictor_Demo ships it, any generative tool, lettering font, master file). Step 2, only after answers: one small CREDITS.yaml at the root of the template's doc_source branch, scoped to the two files the site presents as its identity (LabConstrictor_Logo.png, comic.png), each with creator, rights_holder, licence, note; the site reads it at build through the existing doc_source fetch and fails the build on a malformed file (no silent fallback). Listing all 40 doc_source files is not proportionate; the guide screenshots are the template's own UI. Until the file exists, do not claim anything beyond the existing footer sentence about other projects' logos. Remove or soften the 'hand-drawn' wording in lc.css comment only if owners say it is wrong (it is a CSS comment, not shown to visitors).
verdicts.evidence: git log origin/doc_source in /home/user/LabConstrictor shows four 'Add files via upload' / merge commits by Iván Hidalgo for the logo and comic; ls-tree of doc_source has no LICENSE, README or credits file (grep for licen|credit|readme|font returned nothing). PIL on LabConstrictor_Logo.png (256x256): info Software=www.inkscape.org only. LabConstrictor_Demo/app/logo has its own logo.png. Template README embeds comic.png with no credit. lc.css line 2: 'hand-drawn logo and comic as the illustrations'.

verdicts.misleading_risk: The factual part is right but the wording risks overclaiming. Verified: the NucleiSky banner on the built /apps/nucleisky/ shows a four-point sparkle at bottom right (visible when viewed), and NucleiSky/app/logo holds five files named Gemini_Generated_Image_*. That is strong circumstantial evidence, not proof of generation or of who prompted it, and I cannot verify Google's terms (not fetched). Proposed credit text for the Tools screenshots ('BSD-3 / GPL software') asserts third-party licences that were not verified here and should not be written. 'Claude-assisted test run' is an authorship note about screenshots of software UIs and is not a credit; drop it.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do not add a generic 'credit' field to the manifest schema now: it needs schema, generator, escaping and tests for something a single app needs. Instead, flag it to the NucleiSky owners (outside this site): decide whether the banner and logo are generated, and keep, credit in the NucleiSky README, or replace; the site already shows docs/assets/banner.jpg from their repo, so the fix is theirs and the site follows. If they want a visible credit on the app page, the existing screenshot 'caption' (3-140 chars, already escaped via esc) can carry it with no schema change, e.g. a caption that states the origin they choose. Revisit an 'icon_credit/credit' field only if a second app needs it. For the napari and Fiji hub pictures, nothing to change: they are screenshots of the programs the site already says belong to their owners, and the napari alt text already says 'A prototype'. Do not state licences of napari or Fiji.
verdicts.evidence: Viewed site/assets/shots/nucleisky-1.jpg: sparkle at lower right. git ls-files in /home/user/NucleiSky lists app/logo/Gemini_Generated_Image_*.png/.ico/.icns and docs/assets/banner.jpg. build/snapshot.json NucleiSky manifest: screenshots [{path docs/assets/banner.jpg, caption 'NucleiSky banner.'}], license MIT, doi 10.1242/jcs.265152. schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json lines 40-47: caption already accepted (minLength 3, maxLength 140) and doubles as alt. Tools screenshot commits d8cb724 and others are authored 'Claude'; hubs.yaml napari text says 'prototype', Fiji card says soon.

verdicts.misleading_risk: A fully generated credits table that prints 'Not stated' for most rows would publish an embarrassing, mostly empty page and could imply the site checked rights it did not. Using the GitHub-reported licence of a source repo as the licence of an image is misleading: the repo licence (e.g. MIT on the template) does not necessarily cover its logo or comic, and the site cannot know that. Font origin URL is not recorded in the repo, so it must not be invented. The audit's claim that fetch_guides.py already records per-repo licence is wrong: only catalogue.repo_license (catalogue.py:86) does it, for apps; source repos for guides and images are not fetched as repository metadata.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Defer a generated page. Smaller, safe alternative after G2 answers arrive: add a short static section 'Images and fonts' to an existing page (the Ecosystem note or a short /credits/ page) built by a small function that reads (a) the CREDITS.yaml from doc_source for logo and comic, printing the creator/licence only as written there, (b) a fixed sentence for fonts naming Inter and Bricolage Grotesque as OFL with the shipped LICENSE-inter.txt and LICENSE-bricolage.txt (verified present in site/assets/fonts), (c) the existing sentence that logos of napari, Fiji, QuPath and Google Colab belong to their owners and are shown only to identify them (already in pages_site.py:93 and the footer, overrides/main.html:102). Do not print repo licences as image licences; do not list every file (23 doc images, 7 hubs, etc.). If CREDITS.yaml is absent the build stops (no silent fallback) or the row says 'Not stated' plus a build/problems.md warning, as the owners prefer. Add one test for present and one for missing. Skip DESIGN.md pattern, check_design hook and per-asset provenance plumbing in hubs.py/hosts.py unless the catalogue grows.
verdicts.evidence: site/assets inventory confirmed: fonts/ 4 woff2 plus LICENSE-bricolage.txt and LICENSE-inter.txt; shots/ 1; icons/ 2; hubs/ 7; hosts present. Existing statements found: footer overrides/main.html:102 and pages_site.py:93 ('The logos of napari, Fiji, QuPath and Google Colab belong to their owners and are shown only to identify them'), rendered in site/ecosystem/index.html. grep for 'license' in scripts shows only catalogue.py:86-103 (app repos) and pages_apps.py:145 ('License' row, 'Not stated' fallback already implemented for apps). Largest module is guides.py at 258 lines, so a new credits module is feasible but not needed yet. Site has 6 listed apps and is unlisted (extra.listed false).
